chunks: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us. He said: Abu Yusuf Ya'qub b. Muhammad al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Ibn Umara narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Abi'l Za'za' al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: Abu Thabit Abd al-Karim al-Jazari narrated to us from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Abdullah b. Abbas. He said:
The Prophet (s) became immensely famished, so he went to the Ka'ba, held onto its cloak, and said: Lord of Muhammad! Do not starve Muhammad more than what You have already starved him. He said:

So, Gabriel (as) came down with an almond. He said: O Muhammad! Allah, the Majestic, sends you peace. He said: O Gabriel! Allah is Peace, and peace is from Him, and peace will return to Him. He said: Surely, Allah commands you to break open this almond.

So, he broke it open, and behold, a fresh green leaf appeared, upon which it was written: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I supported Muhammad with Ali, and aided him through him. He does not do justice to himself before Allah who distrusts Allah in His judgment, and impatiently awaits His sustenance.

key_terms.أيدت محمدا بعلي: I supported Muhammad with Ali — divine declaration of Ali's role
key_terms.رزقه: His sustenance — God's provision and livelihood
key_terms.قضائه: His judgment — God's decree and divine will
key_terms.لوزة: an almond — the miraculous vessel for the divine message
key_terms.ونصرته به: and aided him through him — Ali as the instrument of divine support

ai.seo_question: What miracle did Gabriel bring the Prophet Muhammad with an almond?
ai.summary: Abdullah b. Abbas narrates that the Prophet (s), suffering from extreme hunger, went to the Ka'ba and supplicated to God. Gabriel descended with an almond containing a fresh green leaf inscribed with the shahada and a divine declaration that Muhammad was supported by Ali. The leaf also warned against distrusting God's judgment or becoming impatient with His provision. This miraculous narrative was narrated in the assembly of the 11th of Rajab, 368 AH, and emphasizes both the Prophet's trust in God during hardship and Ali's divinely ordained role as the Prophet's support.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us. He said: Abu Yusuf Ya`qub b. Muhammad al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Ibn `Ammara narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Abi’l Za`za` al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: Abu Thabit `Abd al-Karim al-Jazari narrated to us from Sa`id b. Jubayr from `Abdullah b. `Abbas. He said:
The Prophet (s) became immensely famished, so he went to the Ka`ba, held onto its cloak, and said: Lord of Muhammad! Do not starve Muhammad more than what You have [already] starved him. He said:

So, Gabriel (as) came down to him with an almond. So, he said: O Muhammad! Allah recites the salaam to you. So, he said: O Gabriel! Allah is Peace, and peace is from Him, and peace will return to Him. So, he said: Surely, Allah commands you to break open this almond.

So, he broke it open, and a fresh green leaf appeared, upon which it was written: “There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Muhammad is aided and supported by `Ali. Allah does not bless those who distrust Allah in His judgment, and He decelerates their sustenance.”
